title: So you want an Investor and Business Visas for the UAE
body_markdown:
The UAE has become a magnet for founders: strategic location, founder-friendly regulations, and solid infrastructure. If you plan to establish a company, invest in an existing business, or relocate your operations here, one of the first steps is to apply for a visa.


The good news is that the UAE offers several types of visas to choose from to best match your business plan and objectives. This guide covers the different visa options, the UAE's investor visa requirements, and what the government charges for each of them, so you can pick the one that suits your business plans the best.


## What is a UAE business visa?


The UAE business visa is a permit that allows foreign nationals to enter or reside in the country for business-related purposes. That said, it is an umbrella term for several specific types that allow specific activities, such as:


- Exploring business opportunities & attending meetings and conferences.
- Establishing or investing in a UAE company
- Living in the UAE while managing your business.
- Sponsor eligible family members under certain residence visas.


## Types of UAE business and investor visas


The UAE offers several visa options designed for different scenarios:


### Business visit visa


The business visit visa, officially termed the[Visit visa to explore investment opportunities](https://gdrfad.gov.ae/en/services/957ca221-4083-11ed-4fe5-0050569629e8) , is a single-entry visa that can be valid for 60, 90 or 120 days. It's meant for potential business owners exploring commercial opportunities in the UAE. It does not allow the holder to live permanently in the country, but at the same time does not require a sponsor or a host.


### Virtual work residence visa


The Virtual Work Residence Visa is meant for overseas employees and business owners to live in the UAE while continuing to work for companies based outside the country. You can apply for it via the[GDRFA website.](https://www.gdrfad.gov.ae/en/services/64154a31-ec6d-11ec-140b-0050569629e8) To apply for one, you need to provide proof of remote work for an overseas entity, income of at least USD 3,500 a month, and valid health insurance.


### Green visa


The[Green Visa](https://www.gdrfad.gov.ae/en/services/c4d66f28-408c-11ed-4fe5-0050569629e8) provides a five-year self-sponsored residence option for eligible professionals, freelancers, entrepreneurs and investors. As an investor, you must provide proof of capital investment of at least around AED 1 million or based on the specific free zone/authority requirements.


### Golden visa


The Golden Visa is designed for investors, entrepreneurs, exceptional talent and other qualifying individuals seeking long-term residency in the UAE. The[eligibility criteria, per the ICP](https://icp.gov.ae/en/services/uae-golden-residency/) (a minimum AED 2 million investment in the UAE), allow successful applicants to receive up to ten years of renewable residency without requiring a local sponsor.


## Benefits Of Obtaining A UAE Business Visa


The right visa for starting a business in Dubai or elsewhere in the UAE offers several advantages such as:


- **Stable Long-term residency** : Several visa categories for busineses and investors allow you to live in the UAE for several years, which can be renewed if the eligibility requirements continue to be met.
- **Business ownership opportunities:** Depending on your chosen business structure, you can, as a foreign investor, own a business outright in many sectors without requiring a local shareholder.
- **Access to one of the world's leading stable business hubs** : The UAE is a hub for regional and international markets and is backed by several government initiatives to support entrepreneurship.
- **Family sponsorship:** The UAE allows you to easily sponsor your spouse, children, and, in some cases, domestic workers to help you settle in the region comfortably.


## Eligibility to apply for a Dubai business visa


Each UAE business and investor visa has its own eligibility criteria, but most share a few basic requirements. There are, however, the following basic requirements that are common across the four:


- You are a foreign national applying to enter or live in the UAE.
- You are not tied to a UAE employer or host.


The rest are visa-specific:


Type of Visa Who can apply? Key eligibility criteria


Business visit Entrepreneurs, investors and business professionals exploring commercial opportunities Must justify the purpose of the business visit.


Virtual Work Residence Remote employees and business owners working for organisations outside the UAE Must work remotely for a company outside the UAE
Earn at least USD 3,500 per month (or equivalent).
Hold valid health insurance.


Green (Investor/Partner) Investors, partners, entrepreneurs and eligible self-employed professionals A paid-up share of at least AED 1 million in a joint stock company, LLC or partnership


Golden Investors, entrepreneurs and other eligible categories An investment of at least AED 2 million in capital, property, or a business paying at least AED 250,000 in annual taxes.


## UAE investor visa requirements and documents


All the business visas discussed here require the following core documents:


- A recent personal photo
- A passport copy valid for at least six months.
- Valid health insurance (where applicable).
- Medical fitness certificate for residence visas.
- Emirates ID registration or receipt, where applicable.


The remaining documents depend on the specific visa you are applying for:


Type of Visa Additional documents required


Business Visit Proof of investment


Virtual work Proof of remote employment with an organisation outside the UAE.
Proof of a monthly income of at least USD 3,500 (or equivalent).
Valid health insurance.


Green A permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation.
A partnership or investment contract.


Golden Investors: A valid trade licence, certified financial report, company bank statement, tax registration documents, and proof of investment.
Property investors: Proof of property ownership meeting the prescribed value, while deposit investors require proof of qualifying bank deposits.


## Step-by-step guide to applying for a UAE business visa


The exact application process depends on the visa you choose, but the overall journey is roughly the same and goes as follows:


1. Decide which visa suits your objectives.
2. Compare your finances, qualifications, and investment against the specific visa's threshold requirements.
3. [Register your business](https://www.alaan.com/blog/how-to-register-a-company-in-the-uae-step-by-step-guide) , if required.
4. Prepare your supporting documents.
5. Apply through the right channel (ICP Smart Services portal, GDRFA Dubai or the relevant free zone's portal).
6. Complete medical screening and register for an Emirates ID.
7. Receive your residence visa.


## Visa fees and processing timeframes


As of 2026, the fees and processing times of the four visas discussed here are as follows.


Visa Fees Average Processing time


Business Visit 60-day visit visa: AED 200 plus 5% VAT
90-day visit visa: AED 300 plus 5% VAT
120-day visit visa: AED 400 plus 5% VAT 48 hours


Virtual Work AED 200 plus 5% VAT 48 hours


Green AED 200 plus 5% VAT 48 hours


Golden AED 2,800 – AED 4,800 plus 5% VAT 7 - 30 working days.


**Note: T** he table above covers only the cost of the visa itself. Applying from inside the UAE adds additional fees, and you must account for specific visa requirements, such as medical tests, Emirates ID, insurance, and other licence costs.


## Summing it up


The UAE offers several types of visas that cover everything from simply exploring opportunities to pursuing long-term residency through business in the UAE. Before you go ahead, though, it's essential to understand the available visa categories and eligibility requirements for each of them.

## FAQs


**What is the difference between a business visa and an investor visa in the UAE?**


A Business Visit Visa is intended for short-term commercial activities such as attending meetings, networking, or simply exploring business opportunities. An investor visa, on the other hand, is intended to allow eligible individuals to live in the UAE while owning or investing in a business.


**Can I start a business in Dubai with a business visa?**


To start a business in Dubai, you will need to apply for an investor or company owner residence visa after completing company formation. A business visit visa is only meant to allow you to explore business opportunities


**How long does it take to get a UAE business visa?**


Business visit, Virtual Work, and Green visas are typically processed within 48 hours, while the Golden Visa application can take anywhere between 7 and 30 working days. ****


**Can my family join me on a UAE investor visa?**


Yes, your family can join you in the UAE on an investor visa, as long as they meet the relevant sponsorship requirements.
